Name: Event Driven Automation
Author: glowbomb12
Description:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[color=#d4d4d8]After having constant 1 second lagspikes because I had like 20 machines running on the farm (my pc is not a potato), I got tired enough of it and decided to make my own reimplementation of the mod so i can even have 537 furnaces running at once (yes it was loud when they all started on the same tick) without anything noticeably laggy. The result was having machines NOT be polled mapwide every "x" interval and instead have each machine react to specific SMAPI events, therefore making this mod be called "Event Driven Automation".[/color]

[color=#d4d4d8]Because I was essentially remaking the Automate mod's features and mechanics from scratch due to the entirely different concept the mod runs with, I decided to just throw in a bunch of ideas and features that I thought would expand the idea of automation into a good few directions.[/color]

[color=#d4d4d8]To use this mod, you do the same as the original: Place a chest down next to a machine and the machine will pull raw mats from the chest and push products into it. Of course you'll have to wait for each game tick/clock update (10 mins unless you have the Running Late mod or a similar mod enabled and have it set to every minute) to happen before the state is updated and the machines actually push/pull.[/color]

[color=#d4d4d8]Let me know of any bugs, unintended behaviors, and missing features so they can be attended to as best as I can.[/color]

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6 or newer[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0.0 or newer[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] (optional)[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Install[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][url=https://smapi.io/]Install the latest version of SMAPI[/url].[/*]
[*]Unzip the mod folder into Stardew Valley/Mods.[/*]
[*]Run Stardew using SMAPI[/*]
[*]Profit[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Config[/b][/size]
Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] to mess around with the mod's settings.

[size=4][b]Incompatibilities[/b][/size]
[color=#ff0000]Do not run with Automate enabled.[/color] Both mods will try to automate the same machines, producing doubled pushes/pulls and confused states.

[size=4][b]Features[/b][/size]
- All SV 1.6 data-driven machines + Bush, Fruit Trees, Wild Trees, Fish Pond,
  Junimo Hut, Crab Pot, Mill, Hay Hoppers, Auto Grabbers, Garbage Cans, Slime Hutch
- MACHINE GROUPS :D
- Chest and machine priority system (High/Medium/Low/Disabled, input + output independently) by hovering over the chest or machine and pressing either I or O to cycle the respective priority
- Stone Chest with Firewall / Stockpile / Bulk Mode / Type Filter behaviors (plus optional directional flow)
- 20-color smart output routing with 20 categories (Animal Products, Forage & Mushrooms, Artisan Goods, Crafting, Equipment, Museum Items, etc.), configurable as a click-to-toggle grid in GMCM. Optional strict mode keeps rule-bound chests reserved for matching items only
- Gift-safe protection for chests you want excluded from pulls (exact names AND substring keywords)
- Per-save config
- F8 overlay with segmented tiles, per-group colors, fill bars, priorities, and other bits of info
- Diagnostic "unautomated machines" overlay on a separate keybind (default unbound)
- API for other mods to register custom machines/containers or query state
- XP is granted to the player nearest to the machine by default
- Per-machine on/off toggle: hover any machine and press the configured hotkey to disable it from being automated
- Chests in a Slime Hutch will yoink every slimeball inside and get broken up into the actual slime resource as if you manually did it
- Console commands for diagnostics: `aed_status`, `aed_groups`, `aed_stats`, `aed_perf`
- Native compatibility with Producer Framework Mod, Extra Machine Config, Chests Anywhere, Combine Machines Continued, Deluxe Grabber Fix, Machine Upgrade System, Machine Control Panel, Custom Bush, Stardio, Mushroom Propagator
- Other mods' rejection cues (red text, cancel sounds) are muted when AED talks to machines, so no spam every tick
- Translation support: translators drop a locale file (e.g. [i]i18n/es.json[/i]) into the mod folder and SMAPI auto-loads it
- Buildings (like the mill) will pull all of one item type each tick regardless of quality.
- Garden pots automated (crop gets harvested, seeds get planted, fertilizer applied, watering can drains for each pot).

[size=4][b]Advanced[/b][/size]

[center]------Machine groups------[/center]
Machine groups are created when a chest is adjacent to a machine in any of the 8 surrounding tiles (cardinal or diagonal).
You can have multiple groups active at once.
Groups can merge together if you stick a connecting object (chest, machine, etc) between the two and they connect together.
Just like the og Automate mod, specific floors and paths can be set to connect machines and chests together (and propagate the group).

[center]------Stone chest (the gigachad group handoff)------[/center]
Because I was left alone with the different chest types, I realized that one issue I had with the og automate mod is how every machine shared the stuff in my chests and would nab my fruits and fight over how it gets processed. And so I bestowed the stone chests with a few (configurable) stackable features that let you split machine groups and segment production:
[list]
[*][b]Firewall:[/b] The default enabled option. With this on, the stone chest will ignore diagonals and not propagate groups through it. Each cardinal direction will be its own group (unless you connect them together anyways and make this pointless) and is reflected on the overlay.[/*]
[*][b]Stockpile:[/b] The chest keeps a minimum but configurable reserve of every item type held inside of it. Only the surplus above your set amount is available for machines to pull.[/*]
[*][b]Bulk Mode[/b]: Only releases items in batches once your set amount is reached. Useful when you have connected machines that are most efficient running huge numbers at once (*cough* *cough* the mill probably).[/*]
[*][b]Type Filter:[/b] Only accepts item types you've manually put into the chest. Acts as a whitelist, where you just drop in 1 of each item you want to allow, and automation will respect that filter. This also means that you have to manually empty the chest of the item type since it will never remove the last copy of it, hence the "respect" part.[/*]
[/list]Separately, stone chests are able to be made directional by hovering over the chest and pressing the keybind (default unbound) to cycle between the output directions and not having one. Note that this feature requires the Firewall feature to be enabled and the input will always be the opposite side of a directional chest and perpendicular sides are excluded. The overlay reflects this.

[center]------Junimo and Qi Chests (the ender chests of Stardew)------[/center]
I've never used these two in a legit save before, but I figured "why not make them literally be special too?". Both types are on their own networks each, dont propagate groups through the magical link and are just a way to basically have a shared I/O across locations.

[size=4][b]Chest and Machine Input/Output Priority[/b][/size]

Every automated chest and machine has two independent priorities: Input Priority (how AED pulls items out of the chest to feed machines / which machine pulls first when chest inventory is tight) and Output Priority (how AED pushes machine outputs into the chest / which machine pushes its output first when several share the same chests in one tick).
Both default to Medium until altered with "aed_chest_priority" / "aed_machine_priority" or the keybind (the keybind cycles whichever target is under your cursor: chest OR machine). The overlay reflects this in the top corners of each chest and machine tile.
The four levels are:
[list]
[*]High: Use this chest first.[/*]
[/list]On Input: machines pull ingredients from this chest before any other chest.
On Output: machine outputs fill this chest before any other.
[list]
[*]Medium: Default. Used in normal order, after High chests and before Low ones.[/*]
[*]Low: Use this chest last.[/*]
[/list]On Input: machines only pull from this chest if no High or Medium chest has the ingredient.
On Output: this chest only receives outputs after every higher-priority chest is full.
[list]
[*]Disabled: AED never touches this chest in this direction.[/*]
[/list]On Input: machines never pull ingredients out of it (good for "stockpile / save for later" chests).
On Output: machines never put outputs in it (good for chests reserved as input-only or for player storage).

Examples:
[list]
[*]A "feeder" chest you fill with ingredients: leave Input on Medium or High.[/*]
[*]A protected stockpile you don't want machines eating: set Input to Disabled.[/*]
[*]A collection chest you want all outputs funneled into: set Output to High.[/*]
[*]A chest reserved purely for player storage: Disable both.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Console Commands[/b][/size]

Open the SMAPI console (the black window that runs alongside Stardew) and type any of these:                                                                                                                                                                               
[list]
[*][code]aed_status[/code]Prints a one-line summary of how many automation groups exist in each location.[/*]
[*][code]aed_groups[/code]Prints a full breakdown that includes every machine and chest in every group, including their priorities. Use this to confirm a chest and a machine are actually wired into the same group.[/*]
[*][code]aed_stats[/code]Lists every machine type that's pushed an output today, with counts. Handy for confirming things are actually running while you're off doing other stuff.[/*]
[*][code]aed_perf[/code]Shows how long each automation group takes to tick (last/average/max). Use this if you're chasing lag and want to know which corner of the map is the heaviest.[/*]
[*][code]aed_chest_priority <input|output> <High|Medium|Low|Disabled>[/code]Face a chest, then run the command. Sets that chest's input or output priority. Example: "aed_chest_priority output High" makes the chest you're facing be filled before any other chest.[/*]
[*][code]aed_machine_priority <input|output> <High|Medium|Low|Disabled>[/code]Face a machine, then run the command. Same idea as aed_chest_priority but for machines. Controls the order machines pull inputs from / push outputs into shared chests within the same group.[/*]
[*][code]aed_chest_direction <N|E|S|W|none>[/code]Face a stone chest, then run the command. Sets which side outputs and which side accepts input. The arrow points to the output side; the opposite side is the input; the other two sides are blocked. "none" clears it back to bidirectional.[/*]
[*][code]aed_reload_config[/code]Reloads config.json from disk without restarting the game. Useful if you're hand-editing config or copying one in from elsewhere.[/*]
[*][code]aed_forget_priorities[/code]Wipes every chest priority and stone-chest direction across the save. Intended as uninstall hygiene before removing the mod.[/*]
[*][code]aed_test_input <itemId?>[/code]Face a machine, hold the item you want to test (or pass an item id as an argument), then run the command. Reports whether each of the machine's recipes accepts that item, and if not, which rule rejected it and why. Use this to diagnose modded crops/items that aren't being automated.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Multiplayer[/b][/size]
Host-only. Farmhand-exclusive locations are not automated if the host doesn't have the location loaded into their memory; splitscreen does not suffer this limitation.
XP is given to whichever player is physically closest to the machine in the same location. Can be set in the config to only give the host xp, all players get the full amount, or no xp from the automation is given.

[size=4][b]Credits[/b][/size]
Concept and design borrowed from Pathoschild's Automate. This is an independent event-driven reimplementation in the same problem space with new cool stuff added onto it, not a fork or a copy.

Manifest.Name: Event Driven Automation
Manifest.Description: Event-driven version of Automate mod. Machines request items when needed instead of polling, which reduces lag on large scales.
